- scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py: lines 382-383 (_read_review_runs_to_marker stop condition); line 442 (`active = ...`); lines 442-444 (unbound-dispatch listings) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The paging logic in `_read_review_runs_to_marker` stops as soon as a page contains a run with `id <= marker_run_id`. Runs on subsequent pages (all strictly older than the marker) are not read and not present in `branch_runs` / `bound_dispatches`. The `active` list at line 442 does not filter by `run["id"] > marker_run_id`, so it includes any non-completed run from the read pages — including older in_progress dispatches on the marker page — but it never sees older in_progress runs that landed on later pages.
  WHY: On a `claude/*` head with enough churn to push the marker past the first page boundary, an older queued/in_progress `internal-review.yml` dispatch (or an older queued head-branch run) on a subsequent page is silently excluded from `active` and `bound_reviews`. The function returns `None` (the default no-blocker state), and `evaluate()` proceeds to call `scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh` while that older review is still running.

- agents.md: line 1047 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The wording reads “a latest newer completed review of the PR did not conclude `success`”. The implementation computes a unique maximum via `max(newer, key=lambda run: run["id"])`, and the matching paragraph in README.md (lines 1472-1474) correctly uses “the latest newer completed review of the PR”.
  WHY: This is a documentation-only wording inconsistency with no runtime impact.

- agents.md: lines 1047-1048 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workflow list `review_autofix.yml / ai-review.yml / review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml dispatch (no PR binding)` is broken across a line boundary so the workflow names appear on the first line and the qualifier `dispatch (no PR binding)` on the second line, while README.md keeps them together on one line.
  WHY: This is a docs-only line-wrap inconsistency.

- tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py: lines 199-213 (`_malformed` helper using `_DROP = object()` as a sentinel) | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_malformed` calls `run.pop(key)` for fields whose value is `_DROP`. If a future test passes `_DROP` with a key that isn't already present on the run dict, `run.pop` raises `KeyError`.
  WHY: No current runtime impact — the issue is a future-maintenance trap. A minimal fix is `run.pop(key, None)` (one-line, no behaviour change for existing tests).
